analyst_view.overall: Early view: Rennes (17th, 6 points) are unbeaten in Europe but have drawn three of four, and top scorer Esteban Lepaul was out injured in October. Dinamo Zagreb (9th, 7 points) were under an interim coach in early November yet kept clean sheets in both their away games, so this looks closer than the site's strong home-win figure suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, which is high for these two. Rennes' European games have produced seven goals in four (two 0-0 draws) and Dinamo's away games ended 0-0 at Hapoel and 2-0 at Sunderland. Even with Boulaye Dia and Musa Al-Taamari scoring, I'd expect two or three goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, 7.5 of them for Rennes. Dinamo sat deep and countered at Sunderland, which fits a home-heavy count, so I stay near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Dinamo's deep defending can bring bookings, but Rennes' games have been calm, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots. I lean lower: Rennes have not been a high-volume side in Europe (seven goals in four games, two of them 0-0), and Dinamo are comfortable soaking up pressure away from home, as their goalless draw at Hapoel and win at Sunderland showed.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. For the same reasons I lean slightly lower: Dinamo's away clean sheets suggest they limit clear chances, so 8 or 9 looks more likely.
